claims.text: A controlled post-sintering rapid thermal anneal will trigger formation of a fine-scale ductile interfacial phase in the NbMoCrTiAl composite.
The anneal-induced interfacial phase will improve ductility and uniform deformability.
The proposed anneal can preserve the composite's high compressive strength while improving deformability.
The proposed anneal can preserve impact-induced energy release while improving deformability.
The as-sintered NbMoCrTiAl composite contains in-situ-formed TiC and Al2O3 reinforcement particles.
The matrix of the as-sintered NbMoCrTiAl composite contains a BCC solid-solution phase.
The TiC and Al2O3 reinforcement particles are relatively brittle.
The as-sintered composite has a room-temperature compressive fracture strength of approximately 1542 MPa.
The as-sintered composite exhibits cleavage fracture with essentially no room-temperature ductility.
An anneal near 1000°C for five minutes in an inert atmosphere is capable of inducing the proposed ductile interfacial phase.
The proposed phase will form specifically between the BCC matrix and the ceramic reinforcements.
The ductile interfacial phase will facilitate dislocation nucleation and motion and reduce interfacial stress concentrations.
The interfacial phase will provide alternative slip paths, bridge the reinforcement-matrix interface, and blunt deformation-generated crack tips.
Retention of TiC and Al2O3 particles after annealing will continue to reinforce the composite sufficiently to preserve high strength.
Retention of the ceramic particles will preserve impact-induced energy release.
Excessive annealing may cause grain coarsening or an excessive ductile-phase fraction and thereby reduce strength.
Insufficient annealing may produce too little interfacial phase to improve deformability.
The cited fabrication route uses powder processing followed by spark plasma sintering.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing annealed and as-sintered controls using compression, impact, fractography, and interfacial microstructure measurements.
